Florence. A city in central Italy on the Arno River, the birthplace and epicenter of the Renaissance and one of humanity's greatest centers of art, learning, and culture. Home to the Medici banking family and an independent city-state during the Middle Ages and Renaissance, Florence concentrated unprecedented wealth and patronage into art and architecture, producing legendary artists and thinkers who transformed European civilization.

Florence is located in Tuscany in central Italy, situated on the Arno River flowing northwestward toward the Mediterranean. Its strategic position on a crucial river crossing and within the Italian peninsula gave it commercial and cultural advantages. The Medici family, merchant-bankers who rose to prominence in the fourteenth century, became Florence's de facto rulers and became patrons of artists, architects, and thinkers. Their wealth and influence made Florence a beacon of the emerging Renaissance.

The Renaissance, roughly from the fourteenth to seventeenth centuries, was a cultural and intellectual rebirth centered on humanism, the rediscovery of classical texts, and revolutionary artistic techniques. It exploded in Florence and radiated outward to transform all of Europe. Leonardo da Vinci, from fourteen fifty-two to fifteen nineteen, was a painter, sculptor, architect, scientist, and polymath who epitomized Renaissance genius. He created masterpieces including the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper and filled thousands of notebook pages with scientific investigations. Michelangelo Buonarroti, from fourteen seventy-five to fifteen sixty-four, revolutionized sculpture and painting. His marble David from fifteen zero four and his frescoes on the Sistine Chapel ceiling in Rome remain among humanity's supreme artistic achievements.

Florence Cathedral, begun in twelve ninety-six, was crowned by Filippo Brunelleschi's revolutionary dome in the fourteen twenties, a masterpiece of engineering and design that defined Renaissance architecture. The cathedral's dome remains the city's iconic symbol. Florence was an independent city-state and republic with intervals of Medici rule until the sixteenth century, when it was absorbed into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany and eventually the unified Italian state in eighteen sixty-one.
